why: The swatch's narrow opt-out moved onto a CONTAINER, which is the failure mode `forced-color-adjust` invites: the property inherits, so `none` on `.hud-panel` takes every descendant out of colour forcing with it -- the whole interface silently stops honouring the user's high-contrast palette while still passing a rule sweep that only asks whether the declaration exists. Issue #368's boundaries name this explicitly ("No wholesale forced-color-adjust: none") and its criterion 5 requires any use to be narrowly scoped and justified. The justified uses are the swatch, whose inline palette fill is the content, and (issue #630) the selected check's two pseudo-element layers, which must stay opaque and have no descendants. Killed by the guard that names the selector of every use -- a count alone would pass this mutation, since it moves a declaration rather than adding one. Scoped to hud.css.test.ts.
killedBy: forced-colors conformance (issue #368) opts out of colour forcing only on the swatch and the selected check's two layers
